messages:
Maya: FYI opening an escalation for AcmeMedia ticket #C-4832 — they report lots of streaming sessions that tear down abruptly and are being billed. They say it looks like the client closes but we marked 5xx and charged.
Sam (Acme): Yep, we've got ~28% of streaming calls terminating with the socket closed from the client side mid-stream. We never get the final chunk. They show a client-side 'Socket closed by peer' in their runtime logs.
Maya: Can you paste one request-id and any trimmed tcpdump or client logs (FIN/RESET traces)?
Sam (Acme): here's one: req-acme-9c1b. Client snippet:
```
client -> POST /v1/stream (Transfer-Encoding: chunked)
client received chunks up to token 420 then client process did a hard close (SIGKILL) at 2026-03-15T10:22:05Z. client log: 'connection closed: ECONNRESET'
```
Maya: our gateway trace for req-acme-9c1b shows: upstream write failed with "write: broken pipe" and we emitted classify=5xx. Route: hosted-us, model=gpt-redwood-8B, node=gwe-7.
Kevin: can you paste the exact gateway proxy lines (redact IPs)? Also need billing event id so billing team can check charging sequence.
Maya: pasted below (redacted):
```
[gateway] 2026-03-15T10:22:05Z req=req-acme-9c1b flush write error: write tcp 10.2.3.6:443->52.12.34.56:52341: write: broken pipe
[gateway] 2026-03-15T10:22:05Z req=req-acme-9c1b classify=5xx
[billing] 2026-03-15T10:22:05Z charge=req-acme-9c1b tokens=452 billed=true tx=BL-1201
```
Alice: this explains it — our gateway treats write errors during response flush as upstream failure (5xx) by default. Billing currently records charge after model emission completes, before final TCP flush. If the client then aborts, they still get charged and we log a 5xx. Bad UX.
Patrick: I reproduced locally with a small script: open chunked streaming POST, read first few chunks, then close client socket. Gateway logs 502/5xx and billing still shows billed=true. Repro steps:
1) curl -N --data-binary @payload -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream &
2) sleep 2; kill -9 $!
Observed gateway: write error -> classified=5xx.
Kevin: two important questions: (A) were tokens generated and billed before client closed? (B) should we reclassify these errors to a client-abort category (499) so infra isn't blamed and dashboard isn't noisy?
Maya: billing confirms tokens=452 were recorded and billed for tx BL-1201. They can issue refunds but need an engineering signal to automate.
billing-bot: BL-1201 shows billed=true; last_activity=2026-03-15T10:22:05Z; refund_possible=true (manual).
Sam (Acme): we only received up to token ~420. The final bytes (last 32 tokens) never arrived to our edge, so client saw truncated response. Customers expect not to be charged for content they didn't receive.
Alice: engineering suggestion: detect write syscall errno (EPIPE/ECONNRESET) and correlate with kernel connection state to determine if close was client-initiated. If client-initiated, emit a 499-like metric and tag billing event with client_close=true.
Patrick: I built a small reproducer and added a unit test that simulates client FIN during response flush. Repro commands (linux):
```
# quick repro using socat and curl
echo -e 'POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n' > /dev/tcp/api.redwood.ai/443 &
# or: curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --data-binary @payload https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream &
sleep 1; kill -9 $!
```
Kevin: code path analysis: billing hook executes after model emission and before flush. If flush fails we don't roll back billing. We should introduce either a compensating refund workflow or delay billing until flush success — delaying billing hurts accounting and reliability. So pragmatic fix: 1) classify client-initiated write errors as 499 for metrics and 2) add a compensation/refund signal to billing when client_close=true is observed.
Alice: I'll open an infra PR to change classification heuristics and emit an event for billing. We'll also gate auto-refund on account policy (some enterprise customers opt out). Need audit logs to prevent abuse.
Kevin: creating draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/5470 — changes: (a) if write returns EPIPE/ECONNRESET and kernel shows FIN from remote, classify as 499; (b) add client_close flag to billing event; (c) CI e2e test using the reproducer.
Patrick: tested patch on staging. Example staging logs:
```
[gateway] req=req-acme-9c1b flush write: EPIPE -> classified=499 client_close_detected=true
[billing] req=req-acme-9c1b tokens=452 billed=true note=client_close_flag tx=BL-1201
```
Kevin: billing change: if billing event has client_close_flag=true and account.auto_refund=true -> trigger compensating refund and mark charge as compensated. If auto_refund=false -> create ops ticket for manual review. Also add rate-limit to auto-refund to avoid fraud.
Maya: Filed billing ticket BL-998 to refund AcmeMedia for the impacted charges in BL-1201. Customer notified.
Sam (Acme): thanks — can you give ETA for permanent fix so we stop seeing this?
Alice: plan: merge after 24h staging bake and run chaos suites. Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h. ETA to prod: 48 hours.
Kevin: follow-ups list: 1) add synthetic monitor to alert when streaming client-abort rate > 0.5% (alerts to oncall), 2) add docs to streaming best practices warning about abrupt client termination and recommending graceful drain, 3) add dashboard showing compensated refunds vs billing volume.
ops-bot: deployment scheduled: gateway/gwe-7 -> gateway/gwe-7:v2.1.6 on 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
Maya: closing the loop for the customer: refund issued, engineering assigned to PR and rollout, will post follow-up when canary at 25%.
Kevin: post-rollout verification: expect streaming 5xx rate to drop and 499 to rise modestly; token billing delta should show compensations where client_close_flag=true.
Alice: created dashboards: streaming_client_abort_rate, streaming_5xx_vs_499, billing_compensations_by_account.
Maya: thanks for quick turnaround. I'll update AcmeMedia when the 25% canary completes.
Sam (Acme): appreciate the responsiveness, will validate on our side after canary. :thumbsup:
